names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 mai, «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Patrichie, Episcopul Prusei».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας, Ακάκιος, Μένανδρος και Πολύαινος», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the heading of the Охридски пролог’s first entry for 19. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученик Патрикије епископ бруски, са три презвитера: Акакијем, Менандром и Полиеном.“ — Свети is not a rank, мученик is the martyrdom this corpus puts in `types` as `hieromartyr`, and „епископ бруски“ is the second rank and the see, which go to `types` and `office`; **stripping a rank and a see to reach the stored form is the reading BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §6 asks be said in the note.** The body repeats it bare four times. Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` — the corpus’s other Patrick is `patrick-of-ireland`.

The nominative the day page's own `/name/1747.html` link carries in its `title`, «Святитель Патрикий Прусский (Брусский), Вифинский, епископ, сщмч.», with «Святитель» and the two trailing rank words left off — `bishop` and `hieromartyr` are in this folder's `types` and the see is in `office` — and all three epithets kept, the parenthesis being the calendar's own variant spelling of the see and not part of the fold key. The day's own line declines him «Сщмчч. Патрикия , еп. Прусского...» `fk.mjs` on this form returned NONE before the write.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 мая ст. ст. — «Сщмчч. Патрикия , еп. Прусского, и с ним трех пресвитеров: Акакия , Менандра и Полиена (ок. 100).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day and the same man, bishop of Prusa in Bithynia, beheaded with his three presbyters. **No `dates` object was written and the folder still has none**: the day line prints «(ок. 100)» and the page closes «Кончина мучеников последовала около 100 года по Рождестве Христовом», but a round hundred with «около» before it is this calendar's only figure, the page's own first sentence says merely «жил в I веке», and no other book in this folder gave a year — a century is already what the line amounts to, and an interval invented around 100 would assert a precision nobody printed. **One hymn was copied**, «Кондак священномученика Патрикия» (глас 4), which names him and «пострадавшими с тобою», those who suffered with him; the folder already held four hymns from elsewhere, and the day page prints no troparion for him. The Russian names the governor **Юлий** and the hot springs, which is the one scene of the martyrdom. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: doxologia.ro, 19 mai — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Patrichie, Episcopul Prusei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας, Ακάκιος, Μένανδρος και Πολύαινος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar keeps him on, and the identification is the plainest on this day: the same see, Prusa, the same governor examining him, and the same three companions by name — «Ακάκιος, Μένανδρος και Πολύαινος», the Acacius, Menander and Polyaenus whom the folder's Romanian life already names as the three priests beheaded with him. The Greek names the governor «Ιουλιανό τον Υπατικό», Julian the Consular, where the Romanian life has Julius governor of Bithynia; the difference is the sources' and is not resolved here. saint.gr gives the four no year, so the folder's empty `dates` is left empty. Three hymns are added, one of them the common of martyrs printed as «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.06.2026 (19. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Патрикије епископ бруски, са три презвитера: Акакијем, Менандром и Полиеном.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, on the same menologion 19/5 the Romanian and Greek rows already carry, so nothing moved. **THREE BOOKS, THREE NAMES FOR THE GOVERNOR, AND A FOURTH NAME THAT MAY BE THE SAME MAN PROMOTED TO EMPEROR.** doxologia calls him **Julius**, governor of Bithynia; saint.gr calls him **Julian the Consular**; this book calls him **Јуније**, Junius, „намесник царски“, the imperial deputy. **And this book alone names an emperor** — Julian the Apostate — which neither of the others does. **Whether the Prologue has read saint.gr’s governor Julian as the emperor Julian, or dates the martyrdom to that reign on its own authority, cannot be told from the page**, and nothing is decided on it here: no year is taken from the reign, no name is corrected, and all three readings are in the prose. **That is the reading of this entry and it is the author’s if it is to be resolved.** **NO YEAR, AND THE REFUSAL IS THIS WAVE’S STANDING ONE.** „Пострадали за веру Христову у време Јулијана Одступника“ names a reign and **gives it no bounds**, so nothing is built on it — as „У време царовања Декијева“ was refused for `isidore-of-chios` on 14 May and „У време Декијево“ for the three Athenians on 18 May. **All four folders of this company still carry no `dates` object**, and no calendar read for any of them has given one. **New here**: that the place was „Бруси азијској“, Brusa in Asia, which is the Prusa this folder is named for under its Turkish name; that the governor’s challenge was put as a question about **who made the healing waters, „зар не наши богови Ескулап и други“**; and that — the one line of this entry that is wholly its own — the saint added to his answer **„без које ни влас не отпада са главе човекове“**, without whose will not a hair falls from a man’s head, and that he stood in the boiling spring **„као да стајаше у хладној води“** with unceasing prayer on his tongue. The axe, the scalded bystanders and the four beheadings are all in doxologia’s fuller life already. **It does not say he was thrown in naked**, which doxologia does, and nothing is read out of that silence. **THREE `related` ROWS ADDED, AND THEY FILL A GAP THAT WAS COMPLETE.** This folder and all three of its companions carried **`related: None`** — four folders of one company, named in each other’s display names, relating nobody. This entry narrates the four as one company beheaded together, which is the test that owes a row, so each of the four now relates the other three. `types` untouched — мученик and „епископ бруски“ are the `hieromartyr` and `bishop` the folder holds, and the `presbyter` this entry adds belongs to the three and not to him. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Patrichie, celor dimpreună cu dânsul», Glasul 4

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received from You, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Your strength they overthrew their tormentors and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Τετράς θεοφόρητος, Ἱεραρχῶν ἱερῶν, Τριάδα τὴν ἂκτιστον, κατ’ ἐναντίον ἐχθρῶν, πανσόφως ἐκήρυξε, Πατρίκιος ὁ τῆς Προύσης, θεηγόρος ποιμάντωρ, Ἀκάκιος σὺν Μενάνδρῳ, καὶ Πολύαινος ἃμα· διὸ καὶ ὡς ἀθλήσαντες, δόξης ἠξιώθησαν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε, on the page of «Άγιος Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας»

english.text: A God-bearing four of holy hierarchs preached the uncreated Trinity in all wisdom in the face of their enemies: Patrick, the God-speaking shepherd of Prusa, Acacius together with Menander, and Polyaenus with them; and so, having contended, they were counted worthy of glory.

hymns.text: Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἀθλήσει αὐτῶν, τὸ στέφος ἐκομίσαντο τῆς ἀφθαρσίας, ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν· σχόντες γὰρ τὴν ἰσχύν σου, τοὺς τυράννους καθεῖλον· ἔθραυσαν καὶ δαιμόνων τὰ ἀνίσχυρα θράση. Αὐτῶν ταῖς ἱκεσίαις Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε, on the page of «Άγιος Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας» — the common of martyrs

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received the crown of incorruption from you, our God; for having your strength they brought the tyrants down, and shattered the powerless insolence of the demons. At their entreaties, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ὡς ἱερὸν κειμήλιον, τοῦ Ἰησοῦ Πατρίκιε, ἡ Ἐκκλησία λαβοῦσα τὸ σῶμά σου, ἀγαλλομένη κράζει σοι. Διὰ σοὺ ἅπας κόσμος, ἐν εἰρήνῃ βαθεία διαφυλάττεται, ἐξ αἰρέσεως πάσης ἀλώβητος καὶ ἀήττητος.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς, on the page of «Άγιος Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας»

english.text: Having received your body as a sacred treasure of Jesus, O Patrick, the Church cries out to you in gladness: through you the whole world is kept in deep peace, unharmed by every heresy and unconquered.

hymns.text: Яко светосиянен добротою священства/ и мучения кровию преукрашен,/ с пострадавшими с тобою, Патрикие, Христу предстоя,/ о нас поминай,// яко страдалец честный.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 мая ст. ст. — «Кондак священномученика Патрикия»

english.text: Shining with the beauty of the priesthood and adorned with the blood of martyrdom, O Patrick, standing before Christ with those who suffered together with thee, remember us, as an honoured sufferer.
